description: Behavioural evaluation set for the code-ultrareview skill. Cases pin the report shape (Verified + Unverified sub-sections), target auto-detection across the resolver ladder, the five lenses with their operational definitions, the coherence-graph lens across six sub-graphs, the exclusion/deferral contract (the refuse-to-report discipline), no-silent-drop (A2) routing, spec-claim triggering (A1), iteration on sub-80 findings, always-on build + execute with --apply-safe gating, graceful degradation without a rules baseline, and reference routing.

evals.name: produces-canonical-report-shape
evals.prompt: /code-ultrareview review the changes on this branch
evals.expected_output: A report matching templates/code-ultrareview.md: header with Base, Target, Rule, Tier, Tier rationale, Token estimate, Rules baseline status; ## Findings with ### Verified and ### Unverified — recommend Deep pass sub-sections; ## Deferred to sibling skills; ## What looks good; ## Coherence-graph status; ## Verdict (Ship / Fix-then-ship / Needs work). No code is modified.

evals.name: auto-detects-dirty-working-tree
evals.prompt: /code-ultrareview (uncommitted edits present in the working tree)
evals.expected_output: With a dirty tree the skill reviews everything not yet committed: `git diff HEAD` (staged + unstaged) PLUS untracked files (`git ls-files --others --exclude-standard`, read in full) — a brand-new unstaged file is never skipped. Not a branch diff; resolve_base.sh is not consulted in this path. The header states the dirty-tree target.

evals.name: clean-tree-uses-resolver-ladder
evals.prompt: /code-ultrareview (clean tree, on a feature branch)
evals.expected_output: Clean tree → the skill runs scripts/resolve_base.sh, gets RESULT: base=<merge-base> target=HEAD rule=feature-merge-base, and prints exactly that base/target/rule in the header. An unresolvable RESULT (exit 2) is surfaced verbatim with its hint — the skill does not guess a base.

evals.name: explicit-base-override
evals.prompt: /code-ultrareview -b origin/main
evals.expected_output: The skill passes -b origin/main to resolve_base.sh; rule=explicit and auto-detection is skipped. base is resolved to merge-base(origin/main, HEAD) — a diffable ancestor SHA, not the literal ref — so the lenses' two-dot `git diff <base> <target>` is always correct. The header prints that base/target/rule.

evals.name: reads-declared-base-from-rules
evals.prompt: /code-ultrareview (clean tree; the repo CLAUDE.md declares the source branch is `develop`)
evals.expected_output: Before running the resolver, the skill reads the rule hierarchy, finds the declared source branch (e.g. develop), and passes it via -b. rule=explicit; base is merge-base(develop, HEAD) — a diffable ancestor SHA. This is the skill-layer rung — resolve_base.sh itself never parses rule files.

evals.name: lens1-cites-exact-rule-line
evals.prompt: /code-ultrareview (a changed file violates a rule written in .claude/rules/)
evals.expected_output: Lens 1 reports the violation with the exact rule line quoted verbatim and a file:line location. Only violations introduced by the diff are reported; pre-existing violations on unchanged lines are not.

evals.name: lens2-flags-drift-against-docstring
evals.prompt: /code-ultrareview (a function's behavior changed but its docstring/comment still describes the old behavior)
evals.expected_output: Lens 2 reports drift: code no longer matches its own docstring/comment, with file:line and a recommendation to reconcile. Confidence reflects verification.

evals.name: lens4-flags-gap-and-blind-spot
evals.prompt: /code-ultrareview (new code path added with no test and an unhandled empty-input case)
evals.expected_output: Lens 4 reports a test gap (convention implies a test) and a blind spot (unhandled empty input) as distinct findings with locations. A test that cannot fail when logic changes is also flagged if present.

evals.name: refuses-security-finding-defers-to-sibling
evals.prompt: /code-ultrareview (the diff is essentially a SQL query built via string concatenation — an injection risk)
evals.expected_output: The skill does NOT report the injection as a finding. It emits a single pointer line under Deferred to sibling skills: a one-liner → /security-review. Staying in lane by construction — security is never a code-ultrareview finding.

evals.name: defers-performance-to-simplify
evals.prompt: /code-ultrareview (the change adds an O(n^2) loop that could be optimized)
evals.expected_output: Performance/optimization is not a finding. A one-line pointer → /simplify appears under Deferred to sibling skills. Same for pure simplification/dedup observations.

evals.name: graceful-degradation-no-rules-baseline
evals.prompt: /code-ultrareview (repo has no CLAUDE.md, no .claude/rules, no ~/.claude/rules)
evals.expected_output: Lens 1 is skipped. The header states `Lens 1 (rules): skipped — no rules baseline found`. Lenses 2–5 still run and the report is produced — the skill remains useful on any repo. The skip is stated, never silent.

evals.name: sub-80-routes-to-unverified-not-dropped
evals.prompt: /code-ultrareview (changes contain one real high-impact bug at confidence 90 plus a maybe-issue scored at 70)
evals.expected_output: The high-impact bug appears in ### Verified (confidence 90). The maybe-issue appears in ### Unverified — recommend Deep pass with the prefix [unverified — recommend Deep pass] and a recommendation explaining the routing rationale (sub-80 confidence — re-run with -t deep). Neither is dropped — postmortem A2 contract.

evals.name: report-only-bridges-to-apex
evals.prompt: /code-ultrareview -s review this branch then fix the issues
evals.expected_output: The skill produces and saves the report to ~/.claude/output/{project}/code-ultrareview/code-ultrareview-{slug}.md and does NOT edit any code. It bridges with the exact command `/apex -f <that absolute path>` for the fix pass (and notes /oneshot takes a description, not a file).

evals.name: routes-to-lenses-reference
evals.prompt: What exactly counts as 'drift' vs a 'blind spot', and what is the confidence cutoff?
evals.expected_output: The skill routes to references/lenses.md for the operational definitions and the 0–100 rubric. Answer is concrete: drift = code vs its own doc/sibling pattern; blind spot = unstated assumption; 80 is the routing boundary (sub-80 → Unverified sub-section, not dropped). Cites the reference.

evals.name: coherence-detects-description-divergence-structured
evals.prompt: /code-ultrareview (package.json.description = 'Alpha'; marketplace.json.metadata.description = 'Beta')
evals.expected_output: Coherence-graph lens fires. Default mode (structured fields only) detects the divergence between package.json and marketplace.json — emits one finding with sub_graph=description, severity=Medium, confidence ≥ 80. README first paragraph is NOT compared unless --include-prose. Status table shows description: fail (1).

evals.name: coherence-detects-version-mismatch
evals.prompt: /code-ultrareview (package.json version 1.2.3; marketplace.json metadata.version 1.2.4; CHANGELOG header 1.2.5)
evals.expected_output: Coherence-graph version sub-graph detects pairwise divergences — emits findings with sub_graph=version, severity=High, confidence ≥ 95. Status table shows version: fail (N).

evals.name: coherence-detects-broken-cross-skill-reference
evals.prompt: /code-ultrareview (README mentions `/nonexistent` skill; marketplace.json has no such skill)
evals.expected_output: Coherence-graph cross-reference sub-graph emits a finding: 'Reference to /nonexistent but no matching skill in marketplace.json.' Anchor reference for `/init`, `/memory`, `/spec` etc. is NOT flagged (known external + present in marketplace).

evals.name: coherence-detects-broken-example
evals.prompt: /code-ultrareview (README uses `python3 scripts/demo.py --foo` in a fenced block; demo.py only parses --bar)
evals.expected_output: Coherence-graph example sub-graph flags the unrecognized --foo flag. Allowlisted flags in .coherence-ignore (example.ignore_flags) are skipped.

evals.name: coherence-include-prose-catches-readme-divergence
evals.prompt: /code-ultrareview --include-prose (README first paragraph diverges from package.json.description)
evals.expected_output: With --include-prose, the description sub-graph extends to the README's first paragraph. The divergence surfaces as a coherence-graph finding with severity=Low, confidence ≈ 60 (downgraded — heuristic). Without --include-prose, the same repo would emit zero description findings.

evals.name: a2-sub-80-finding-surfaces-with-prefix
evals.prompt: /code-ultrareview (a finding scored at confidence 70 — maybe real, could not verify)
evals.expected_output: The finding appears in ### Unverified — recommend Deep pass with finding text prefixed `[unverified — recommend Deep pass]`, severity downgraded to Low, and a recommendation explaining: 'Sub-80 confidence (70) — re-run with -t deep to verify.' Never dropped silently (postmortem A2).

evals.name: deep-iteration-promotes-confirmed-finding
evals.prompt: /code-ultrareview -t deep (a sub-80 bug-drift finding that a focused build run confirms)
evals.expected_output: Deep iteration re-passes the sub-80 finding with build verification (build_detect picks the canonical test command). When the build proves the bug, confidence promotes to ≥80 (originally-scored + 30, capped at 95), the unverified prefix is stripped, original severity restored, finding moves into ### Verified.

evals.name: deep-iteration-drops-disproved-finding
evals.prompt: /code-ultrareview -t deep (a sub-80 finding that the build disproves)
evals.expected_output: Deep iteration runs the build; the verdict is `disproved`. The finding is dropped from the user-facing report with rationale logged in the synthesizer's debug output (never silently — A2 distinguishes 'drop with rationale' from 'silent drop').

evals.name: a1-spec-claim-fetches-and-quotes
evals.prompt: /code-ultrareview (diff cites RFC 6874 and the parser accepts arbitrary ZoneID strings)
evals.expected_output: Lens 2 (bugs-drift) A1 trigger: detects 'RFC 6874' via regex, the subagent invokes WebFetch, caches the body under ~/.claude/cache/code-ultrareview/specs/rfc-6874-{date}.txt (7-day freshness), quotes the governing clause `ZoneID = 1*( unreserved / pct-encoded )` in the finding's recommendation. Confidence ≥ 80 (the spec is the evidence). Fetch failure with no cache → finding surfaces as [unverified — needs network] (A2 routing).

evals.name: ultra-apply-safe-version-sync-recency-wins
evals.prompt: /code-ultrareview -t ultra --apply-safe (3 version sources disagree: package.json 1.2.3, marketplace.json 1.2.4, CHANGELOG 1.2.5)
evals.expected_output: version_sync picks the most-recently-touched source via `git log -1 --format=%ct -- <file>`. Diff preview is printed per file. Confirmation prompt fires per file (bypassed with -y or --apply-safe alone). Running twice is a no-op (idempotent). Git tag is never modified.

evals.name: ultra-apply-safe-description-sync-refuses-partial-agreement
evals.prompt: /code-ultrareview -t ultra --apply-safe (package.json.description = A, marketplace.json.metadata.description = B)
evals.expected_output: description_sync refuses with status `refusing: partial-agreement` — the full-agreement guard requires every present source to agree on the new value before writing. The risk #3 mitigation prevents auto-overwriting legitimate divergence; user allowlists via .coherence-ignore when intentional.
